verses.text: In the twelfth year that Ahaz was king of Judah, Hoshea son of Elah became king of Israel in Samaria. He ruled for nine years.
He did what was evil in the LORD's eyes, but not as much as the kings of Israel before him.
Shalmaneser king of Assyria attacked Hoshea. Hoshea became his servant and paid him taxes every year.

But the king of Assyria found out that Hoshea was plotting against him. Hoshea had sent messengers to So king of Egypt, and he had stopped paying taxes to the king of Assyria as he used to do each year. So the king of Assyria arrested Hoshea and put him in prison.
Then the king of Assyria invaded the whole land. He marched to Samaria and surrounded it for three years.

In the ninth year that Hoshea was king, the king of Assyria captured Samaria. He took the Israelites away to Assyria and settled them in Halah, at the Habor River in Gozan, and in the towns of the Medes.

All this happened because the Israelites had sinned against the LORD their God, who had brought them up out of Egypt and rescued them from the power of Pharaoh king of Egypt. They worshipped other gods.
They followed the customs of the nations the LORD had driven out ahead of them, and the customs the kings of Israel had started.
The Israelites secretly did things against the LORD their God that were not right. They built high places for themselves in all their towns, from the smallest watchtower to the biggest walled city.
They set up sacred stone pillars and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every green tree.
They burned incense at all the high places, as the nations the LORD had driven out ahead of them had done. They did wicked things that made the LORD angry.
They worshipped idols, even though the LORD had told them, "You must not do this."

The LORD warned Israel and Judah through all his prophets and seers. He said, "Turn from your evil ways. Keep my commands and laws, following all the Law I commanded your ancestors and sent to you through my servants the prophets."
But they would not listen. They were as stubborn as their ancestors, who did not trust the LORD their God.

They rejected his laws and the covenant he had made with their ancestors, and the warnings he had given them. They followed worthless idols and became worthless themselves. They copied the nations around them, even though the LORD had commanded them not to do what those nations did.
They turned away from all the commands of the LORD their God. They made two metal idols shaped like calves, and an Asherah pole. They worshipped all the stars in the sky, and they served Baal.
They sacrificed their sons and daughters in the fire. They practised fortune-telling and witchcraft. They gave themselves over to doing what was evil in the LORD's eyes, and made him angry.
So the LORD was very angry with Israel, and he removed them from his presence. Only the tribe of Judah was left.
But even Judah did not keep the commands of the LORD their God. They followed the customs Israel had started.
So the LORD rejected all the descendants of Israel. He punished them and handed them over to raiders, until he had thrown them out of his sight.
When the LORD tore Israel away from David's family, they made Jeroboam son of Nebat their king. Jeroboam led Israel away from following the LORD and made them commit a great sin.
The Israelites kept on doing all the sins Jeroboam had done. They did not turn away from them,

until the LORD removed Israel from his presence, just as he had warned through all his servants the prophets. So the Israelites were taken from their own land as prisoners to Assyria, and they are still there today.

The king of Assyria brought people from Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath, and Sepharvaim, and settled them in the towns of Samaria in place of the Israelites. They took over Samaria and lived in its towns.
When they first lived there, they did not worship the LORD. So the LORD sent lions among them, and the lions killed some of them.

Someone reported to the king of Assyria, "The people you took away and settled in the towns of Samaria do not know what the god of that land requires. So he has sent lions among them, and the lions are killing them, because the people do not know what he requires."
Then the king of Assyria gave this order: "Send back one of the priests you took away from there. Let him go and live there and teach the people what the god of the land requires."
So one of the priests who had been taken away from Samaria came back and lived in Bethel. He taught them how to worship the LORD.
But each nation still made its own gods. They set them up in the shrines on the high places the people of Samaria had made, each nation in the towns where it lived.
The people from Babylon made Succoth Benoth. The people from Cuthah made Nergal. The people from Hamath made Ashima.
The Avvites made Nibhaz and Tartak. The Sepharvites burned their children in the fire as sacrifices to Adrammelech and Anammelech, the gods of Sepharvaim.
They worshipped the LORD, but they also chose all kinds of their own people to be priests at the high places. These priests offered sacrifices for them in the shrines.
They worshipped the LORD, but they also served their own gods, following the customs of the nations they had been taken from.

To this day they still follow their old customs. They do not truly worship the LORD. They do not obey the laws, rules, teachings, and commands the LORD gave the descendants of Jacob, whom he named Israel.
The LORD had made a covenant with the Israelites and commanded them, "Do not worship other gods. Do not bow down to them, serve them, or offer sacrifices to them.
Worship only the LORD, who brought you up out of Egypt with great power and a mighty arm. Bow down to him and offer sacrifices to him.
Always be careful to obey the laws, rules, teachings, and commands he wrote for you. Do not worship other gods.
Do not forget the covenant I made with you, and do not worship other gods.
Instead, worship the LORD your God. He will rescue you from the power of all your enemies."
But they would not listen. They kept on following their old customs.
So these nations worshipped the LORD, but they also served their idols. Their children and grandchildren still do the same as their ancestors did, to this day.
